title: Code Review is now generally available
summary: Claude Code's automatic PR review is now generally available for Team and Enterprise. Reviews run about 3x faster than preview (roughly 6-10 minutes versus about 20), with more concise findings and more bugs that matter caught, and admins can set each repo to Quick, Standard (default), or Deep review. Eligible Enterprise orgs can claim at least $10,000 in credits by January 15, 2027.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: Anthropic published a reference implementation of scheduled agents on Claude Managed Agents (beta), including a sample daily-brief agent that reads Slack and GitHub and posts a brief to Slack, with code in anthropics/claude-quickstarts. It guards against coverage gaps and repeats, silent source failures, duplicate posts, and date or time zone errors, using a cron schedule, a per-run budget cap, a read-only preferences store, and vaulted credentials. Users start with claude update and /claude-api managed-agents-onboard, though prompt injection in source text remains a caveat.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
summary: Anthropic describes Scion, its in-house source control system, and Antique, its code review tool, built for its large monorepo after the monorepo moved from git to Scion in about five months. Servers handle history, commits, and merges while clients fetch only the files they need and are assumed to be always online, mostly agents and CI. Daily merges grew from about 2,500 to over 30,000, and Anthropic reports roughly 200x lower infrastructure footprint and 100x faster checkouts, though it is not a general git replacement.

title: How the Claude Code team does code review
summary: Anthropic explains how the Claude Code team reviews code now that agents write about 90% of its codebase. Review runs continuously from before a PR exists, an AI reviewer checks every PR, and human approval scales with risk (none for low, one for medium, two for high). From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled, reverts fell by over 40%, and substantive AI comments rose from 16% to 54%, though the team still has no circuit breakers for rising revert rates.

title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests
summary: Block's Bradley Axen describes using Claude Fable 5 to orchestrate company-wide migrations across thousands of PRs, delegating edits and tests to Opus and Sonnet. Model choice is treated as an optimization, with frontier models for planning and cheaper models for routine work, and merges to main and prod deploys still require two human approvals that Claude refuses to bypass. It illustrates how multi-agent orchestration makes cost and oversight central concerns.

title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Claude adds two beta features: live dashboards that connect to BigQuery, Databricks, Snowflake, and Salesforce and auto-update with numbers linked to their queries (paid plans), and Claude Motion, which turns a prompt into editable code-built animated explainers exported as MP4 (Team and Enterprise). Docs, Slides, and Design have left beta and are available on all plans including Free, with the standalone Design site remaining until Dec 14. This lets non-technical staff get data answers and presentations without SQL or tickets.
